L1-FATHOM-FULL48-QUARTER-PULSE.text:
Fathom-authored full-route quarter-pulse realization for the finite 108 printed Level1 exercises.
Scope is exactly the 108 source identities and existing item/module pairs in Results/manager-resume-r01/level001-whole-contract/case-bindings.jsonl, SHA256 9fbcbf1ac7b30b6f55ad4ebf8978f886b14203c68cf34076f8eed99119906717.
The original source supplies fifth-position finger/fret patterns, low E to high e followed by high e to low E, and strict alternate picking without a prescribed initial stroke.
Reuse each reviewed record's 48 existing occurrences in exact array order. Preserve the printed four-finger order within every string, including descent. Keep the four high-e contacts on each side of the turnaround as separate occurrences.
Original source events retain null onset and duration, unresolved timing, all original identities, and the four unchanged 24-contact directional variants. This supplement does not reinterpret or retime those source objects.
For each new full-route variant only, assign one quarter-note unit to every contact: zero-based contact i begins at i/1 quarters, lasts 1/1 quarter, and the complete route ends at quarter 48. This uniform pulse is Fathom-authored practice timing, not an original printed rhythm.
Learners explicitly choose a visible downstroke-start or upstroke-start full-route variant and confirm that choice before launch. For D-start, even zero-based contacts emit D and odd contacts emit U. U-start is the inverse.
The continuous emitted parity applies through string boundaries and the turnaround. Contacts 24 to 25 are U to D for D-start and D to U for U-start. An internal calculation reset that emits the identical sequence is equivalent; an actual repeated or inverted stroke is incorrect.
The existing even_subdivision projection uses notes_per_beat 1, beat_unit_q [1,1], and marking_factor [1,1], on copies of the selected source events. Per-contact hand direction requires separate explicit validation; a technically renderable native model alone does not prove it.
No rest, tail pause, extra repeat, swing, accent, fixed BPM, meter, count-in, acoustic note-off, success threshold or learner performance is authored. Tempo remains a separate learner setting.
New full-route variants are separately identified; old half-route variants remain unchanged and read-only. This supplement creates no event, item or module identity, rewrites no historical Attempt, and supplies no automatic mastery, credit or whole-task completion.
